# v0.26.0 — host message identity (#643, shadow) plus identity fixes (#534, #821, #851, #759, #387)

Qualified at the release candidate tag `v0.26.0-rc1` (`8396706d`): this GA tree is that tree plus this file (RELEASE-READINESS-V1; `git diff --name-status v0.26.0-rc1..v0.26.0` = only this file).

GA acceptance (shadow agreement at least 99% over at least 200 counted bindings in at least 24 h; every disagreement explained with row evidence; durable shadow errors 0; no respin-bar defect that managed profiles can reach): The reference agent's shadow window on an upstream host that stamps `message_uid` (2026-10-06T05:03:29Z → 2026-10-07T05:05:10Z, 24.0 h) agreed on 363 of 363 counted bindings (483 of 483 checked), with 0 unexplained, durable shadow errors 0 and no respin-bar log signal: PASS. The counted bar was met by a disclosed synthetic ACP session on the same agent and candidate; the 61 counted bindings added after that session came from organic traffic, all in agreement. The gauntlet's live soak on an upstream host that stamps `message_uid` agreed on 61 of 61 counted bindings (86 of 86 checked) through 19 committed compactions, a restart and a re-paste.

Minor release on top of `v0.25.1` (`f47b55e0`). Theme: host message identity, in SHADOW mode.
- Upstream Hermes now stamps each message with a `message_uid`. On such a host, LCM records which stored row each uid
  belongs to and counts how often that agrees with its existing identity matching.
- **Ingest, replay and emission decisions are unchanged:** shadow mode only observes.
- **Hosts without the uid feature** (every managed profile's runtime today) see no new key and no new behaviour. LCM
  mints an engine uid only when the host declares `message_uid` persistence-only and the session's lineage resolves.
- No tool name or count changed (15 tools); `LCM plugin loaded` and every `lcm_*` name are unchanged.
- **New setting:** `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=off|shadow|on`, default `shadow`.
  - `on` is reserved and behaves as `shadow`. An unknown value means `shadow`, with one warning.
  - `off` captures nothing, writes nothing and logs nothing.
- **Store:**
  - no schema version change (schema 5) and no new column;
  - one droppable side table, `host_uid_bindings`, created lazily on the first binding write (host or engine uid),
    which happens only on a host with the uid feature;
  - a rollback to `v0.25.1` is plugin-only. CI runs the `v0.25.1` and `v0.25.0-rc1` readers against stores this code
    wrote (#886), including a store with host uids on its rows (#889).
- No change below deletes a stored raw row.
- This release never moves a deployed pin by itself. A deployment moves only when its operator re-pins it.

## Changes since v0.25.1

- **#643 (#835, #837, #838, #839): host message identity, shadow.**
  - **Bindings.** At ingest, each uid-bearing host row is classed after the existing identity decision: skipped,
    composite or remainder, bound, or unbound. Canonical and version bindings record their first replay check
    (agree or disagree); engine and alias-candidate bindings do not enter the gate.
    `/lcm doctor` reports `host_uid_gate_checked/agree/disagree` and the `host_uid_*` counters.
  - **Emit carry (#838).** LCM's own emit path keeps the host's uid where it rebuilds a row:
    - adjacent-assistant merges;
    - ignored-message placeholders;
    - over-cap tool stubs;
    - the cached replay prefix.

    The host therefore does not re-mint a uid for a row LCM only reshaped. A new identity key is written only when
    the host declares `message_uid` persistence-only (checked once per process; fails closed). Provider-visible bytes
    are unchanged.
  - **Engine uids (#839).** Rows LCM generates carry a deterministic uid, so LCM recognises its own rows after a
    restart: summary and objective rows, generated context, proactive recall, the overflow note and placeholder, the
    survival summary row, and the omitted marker. A re-presented engine row is classed GENERATED.
  - **Hygiene (#837).** Deleting messages also deletes their bindings. The lineage key is namespaced by Hermes home.
  - **Fail-open.** Every shadow step catches, counts and continues. Tests compare every `messages` and relation column
    between `off` and `shadow` on the same input.
- **#534 (#850, partial): a forced-overflow recovery note that the proof covers binds back to its emission.** The
  remaining cases keep #534 open.
  - Recovery now records its generated rows as emission descriptors.
  - An echoed note, or the host's merge of the previous user turn with the note, binds back to the emission by digest
    and position, never by content alone.
  - When the retained user row, the latest reply and the note all fit, the reply between them is kept, as the host's
    own compressor keeps it.
- **#821 (#877): a held composite after a crash on rotation is no longer stored twice.** This re-lands #845, which
  #860 reverted, with two guards:
  - older re-sequenced rows are readmitted only as ONE whole composite that LCM itself recorded;
  - no split happens when the remainder's own newer occurrence is in the same view.

  Rotation-only, so it was not reachable on profiles that compact in place.
- **#851 (#879): an older unstamped row can no longer stand in for a composite constituent.** An unstamped stored row
  may serve as a constituent only inside its donor's run: back-to-back user rows of one session and conversation (a
  blank legacy conversation id joins any), within 256 store ids. Any other stored row between them ends the run.
  When the filter rejects a row, the composite or the remainder is stored, so no turn is lost.
- **#891 (#892): a branch no longer inherits its parent's rows.** On a host that rotates sessions, the identity
  anchor treated a compression-ended parent of a branch as an ancestor and matched the branch's copied rows to the
  parent's rows; both sessions summarised them. No row was lost or duplicated. The walk now stops at a fork child,
  as the host-uid walk does. Rotation-only.
- **#759 (#883): one privacy-refused document no longer stops a cloud embedding backfill.** Refused documents are
  withheld before dispatch and stay pending (an uncertain retry keeps its in-flight marker); the rest of the window is
  embedded. An apply run that withheld documents reports `partial` with a `privacy_withheld` count, unless it also
  failed; a dry run keeps `dry-run`. Withheld text never reaches the provider.
- **#387, #882 (#884): stored vectors with an older privacy revision no longer break recall.**
  - `lcm_recall` answers from full text, for every `include`, marked `degraded` with an `embedding_identity_stale:`
    reason. Before, it raised the embedding-privacy error.
  - `lcm_grep` semantic mode falls back the same way.
  - `lcm_doctor` warns with the remedy: `/lcm embed warmup`, then `/lcm embed backfill --apply`.
  - An invalid privacy policy still raises.
  - **#888 (#890):** `lcm_doctor` also checks the chunk identity once the store holds chunk vectors that recall
    can use, and `stale_tasks` names each stale corpus. A summaries-only recall falls back to full text when the
    summary identity goes stale between the check and the scan.
- **#827 (#830): payload lookup index.**
  - Set buckets replace the quadratic bucket build.
  - There is one fallback glob per digest per scope.
  - The stub-first trial and its final assembly share one directory listing.

- **#834 (contributed): chunk vector loading.** With NumPy, float32 chunk vectors load straight into the search matrix;
  NumPy stays optional. Both chunk loaders reject a malformed stored value instead of decoding it.

## Known follow-ups

- **`on` mode (slice C) is deferred.** A host uid will decide identity only after the shadow window shows agreement,
  and once a deployed host carries uids. The identity ledger (`docs/identity-ledger.md`, #893) records a decision for
  each of the 460 existing identity rules, and the entry conditions for `on`. In short, a uid replaces only the matching
  rules; the persisted records that a plugin-only rollback reads keep being written.
- **#844:** the shadow merge-proof walk is not yet bounded. Across 160 local reliability sessions on an upstream host
  (about 17,900 bound uids) it never occurred; the shadow window watches for it.
- **#534:** the cases #850 does not cover stay open.
- **#588:** a fresh bind can re-store already-stored rows. Duplicates only, pre-existing since v0.24.x; host uids give
  the direct check.
- **#7:** the ingest cursor can re-store tool rows; the strict-xfail acceptance set is #742.
- **#885:** an embedding backfill window made only of privacy-withheld rows stalls at that `--limit`; raise `--limit`.
- **#881:** a long question near the full-text arm budget with embeddings on.
- **#887:** a summaries-only `lcm_recall` with the embedding provider down returns no hits instead of full text.
- **#895:** a privacy revision registered between the query check and the vector scan makes a summaries-only `lcm_recall` return no hits instead of full text (pre-existing; embeddings on only).
- **#896:** the doctor's stale chunk-identity remedy omits `--corpus`.
- **#899:** a single message over 3,000 characters that forms a leaf on its own can be stored as a level-3 "verbatim"
  leaf holding the clipped text, so its middle is missing from that summary. The raw rows stay intact and `lcm_expand`
  reaches them. Closes by construction with the summariser input change (#611) in v0.27.0.
- **#646:** with the opt-in summary prompt v2 (`LCM_SUMMARY_PROMPT_VERSION=2`), depth-1 condensations often overrun
  their output cap and can hold compaction; while it is held, survival fits move older rows out of live context (they
  stay stored and searchable). Keep prompt v2 off until v0.27.0; the default prompt is 1.
- **#897:** in a narrow race the shadow side table's readiness flag can be cached before the table commits; shadow counting then stops until the next restart (uid hosts only; no stored-row effect).
- **#921, #922, #923:** in one user turn with a long tool loop, the first compaction can be refused by the host as larger than its input. LCM then holds automatic compaction below its 0.85 survival ceiling for the rest of the turn (#922). A second assembly in the same turn can drop the user request from live context, while it stays stored (#921). After such a turn, the host's rewrite of the head row can store the prompt again (#923; duplicates only).
  All three are pre-existing and identical on v0.25.1. They were found by the new first-request continuity cell (#914). Fixes for #921 and #923, and for #922's refusal, are planned for v0.27.0; a shorter in-turn hold is tracked in #926. #923 needs an unstamped user row, and the gateway stamps every user row on current hosts (none unstamped on the reference agent since 2026-09-24).
- **#937:** in a delegated child (a `delegate_task` subagent), the host-fallback compressor can be built without the
  model or context window. The child then does not compact proactively and can reach an over-window request. Its
  fallback summary call can also name the model "unknown". Pre-existing and identical on v0.25.1; the fix is planned as a
  v0.26.1 patch.

## Benchmark boundary

- The qualification is identity correctness and lifecycle reliability on real hosts. The recall scorecard above is a
  release-over-release retrieval check, not an answer-accuracy claim. The QA re-baseline (LongMemEval-S, LoCoMo)
  runs on the v0.26.0 GA in its own track (milestone H2).

## Upgrade

- **Install:** plugin only. Verify the exact commit, install this tag at it and restart the gateway. No manual
  migration: the `host_uid_bindings` side table is created automatically on the first binding write.
- **Rollback:** to `v0.25.1`, plugin only. The side table can stay; `v0.25.1` ignores it.
- **Settings:** none needed. To opt out of shadow observation, set `LCM_HOST_MESSAGE_UID=off`.
